title: Redemptorist Water Channel cleared of 748 tonnes of garbage
summary: The trash trap at the entrance of the Redemptorist Water Channel in Parañaque broke during monsoon rains and high tides, letting debris from Manila Bay pile up in the narrow waterway. The MMDA hauled 748.87 metric tons of garbage and debris, about 203 truckloads, from the channel between 10 and 14 August 2026. The waste was trucked to landfills in San Mateo and Rodriguez, Rizal, and MMDA General Manager Nicolas Torre III said the major bulk of trash had been collected.

timeline.note: Clearing operations began after the channel's trash trap broke and tides pushed waste into the waterway.
Five-day operation ended with 748.87 metric tons removed, and the MMDA said only smaller waste remained.

title: Court halts Guindarohan quarry over imminent landslide risk
summary: On 4 May 2026 Judge Dennis C. Larrobis of Regional Trial Court Branch 76 issued a 72-hour Temporary Environmental Protection Order directing Jomara Konstruckt Corporation and Jomara Agri Foods and Supply Corporation to stop all excavation and removal of soil, rocks, sand and gravel in Barangay Guindarohan, Minglanilla. The petition by 13 residents said families within 60 meters of the excavation zones were at grave risk of death from landslides; 18 families had already been evacuated in 2022. The Mines and Geosciences Bureau had documented ground cracks since December 2021 and inspectors found unsafe high-wall cuts as deep as 15 meters, with a summary hearing on extending the order set for 6 May.

timeline.note: MGB began documenting ground cracks in Guindarohan and later confirmed weak, weathered soil.
72-hour TEPO ordered the two Jomara companies to stop quarrying, excavation, land clearing, tree cutting and heavy equipment use.
Summary hearing scheduled to decide whether the halt would be extended while the environmental case proceeds.

sources.title: Court halts Minglanilla quarry operations due to 'imminent' landslide risk

title: Expanding sinkhole in Bogo City flagged as high-risk
summary: A cover-collapse sinkhole was first reported at 4:45 a.m. on 20 August 2026 in Sitio Indilicio, Purok Libog 1, Barangay Guadalupe, Bogo City. MGB-7 assessed it on 22 and 23 August, measuring it at about 15 by 25 meters with an estimated cavity depth of around 15 meters, and found it had widened by roughly two meters with continuing rim collapses, rumbling sounds and groundwater flow; the nearest house was 18 meters from the rim. In a 24 August advisory the bureau classified the site a high-risk ground collapse area and recommended a 20-meter no-entry zone and a 50-meter controlled-access zone, with pre-emptive evacuation during heavy rain.
referredTo: Mines and Geosciences Bureau Region VII

timeline.note: Sinkhole first reported at 4:45 a.m. in Sitio Indilicio, Barangay Guadalupe.
Field and ground-penetrating radar surveys measured the sinkhole at about 15 by 25 meters and found it still expanding.
Advisory classified the area as high-risk and recommended 20-meter no-entry and 50-meter controlled-access zones.

title: Jaro River clean-up hauls 74 tonnes of trash in two weeks
summary: Iloilo City launched Oplan Kontra Baha on 19 May 2026 with DOLE-6 and DPWH-6, deploying 70 TUPAD workers for a 31-day clean-up of the heavily silted and waste-clogged Jaro River from Hinactacan and Ticud in La Paz to Tabuc Suba in Jaro. By 2 June, 74 tons of waste had been collected, with the stretches in Ingore, Ticud and Baldoza completed and the operation 75 percent done. General Services Office head Neil Ravena called the volume alarming and projected the total could exceed 100 tons, with waste traps planned for Banuyao, Caindir, Hinactacan and Tabuc Suba.

timeline.actor: Iloilo City Government with DOLE-6 and DPWH-6
timeline.note: Oplan Kontra Baha launched with 70 TUPAD workers for a 31-day clean-up of the Jaro River.
74 tons of waste collected so far, operation 75 percent complete and projected to exceed 100 tons.

title: Guisad Surong landslide kills 10, Baguio pursues no-build zone
summary: At about 7:20 p.m. on 9 August 2026, after relentless rains from the enhanced southwest monsoon, a slope collapsed at Sitio Riverside, Purok 2, Barangay Guisad Surong, Baguio City, destroying three houses; 10 people died and three survived, and 21 families of about 70 people were displaced. Search and retrieval ended at 2:50 a.m. on 11 August. The site is on MGB hazard maps as landslide-prone, and after clearing began on 18 August Mayor Benjamin Magalong moved to declare the area a no-build zone and to study slope stabilization with MGB and DPWH; another slide hit Purok 3 on 3 September, affecting one house and forcing six people to relocate.
referredTo: Baguio City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office

timeline.note: Slope at Purok 2 collapsed onto three houses at about 7:20 p.m.; four people were extracted immediately.
Search and rescue concluded at 2:50 a.m. with 10 dead and three survivors.
Clearing of the landslide area began and the mayor moved to declare Guisad Surong a no-build zone.
A new landslide at Purok 3 affected one house and six people were moved to safer areas.

title: Two miners killed in Surigao City small-scale mining landslide
summary: A landslide buried a small-scale gold mining site in Sitio Periko in the uplands of Surigao City on 29 January 2026, killing two miners and seriously injuring a third, all of Barangay Anomar. The three were manually digging soil and rock for sluice mining, locally called banlas, and police said the tunnel collapsed after several consecutive days of heavy rain; one report places the site in Barangay Anomar and another at Purok Tagbunuan, Barangay Mabini. The Bureau of Fire Protection, CDRRMO, PNP and Army responded, the city council took up regulations on illegal mining, and Surigao City police continued investigating, including the identity of any financiers.

timeline.note: Landslide at the banlas mining site killed two miners and seriously injured a third; BFP, CDRRMO, police and Army responded.
Police investigation continued to establish the cause and identify financiers of the illegal mining operation.
